intent: Weld-up trailer hitch frame: a 2-in square steel shank (z 8–10, centred y=0, x 9 to -57) plus a ladder on top (z 10–12) with two rails at y=±30 and front/back cross members, all unioned into one solid.

feedback: The ladder runs too far forward: the two rails and the cross members must only sit under the box, between x = -18 in and x = -57 in, with the front and back cross members inside that span (not overhanging it). Only the shank continues forward into the receiver to x = 9 in.

Close, but the ladder is still 1 in too long at each end: it spans x = -58 to -17 in and should span exactly -57 to -18 in. Put the cross members' outer faces flush with those ends (front member from x = -20 to -18, back member from x = -57 to -55) and stop the rails at the same ends.

Add a riser so the box floor ends up 18 in off the ground. Keep the lower shank in the receiver at z = 8 to 10 in, but only from x = 9 in back to x = -8 in. Add a vertical 2 in square riser post at x = -8 to -6 in, from z = 8 to 16 in. Then an upper shank at z = 14 to 16 in, from x = -8 in back to x = -57 in. Move the ladder (rails and cross members) up to sit on it, from z = 16 to 18 in, still between x = -18 and x = -57 in. It must stay one solid.

Rebuild the frame from real square steel tube (hollow, open ends) instead of solid bars, keeping the layout. Give each group its own tube size in PARAMS: shank_w / shank_t for the lower shank in the receiver (2 in, 1/4 in wall), riser_w / riser_t (2 in, 1/8 in), upper_w / upper_t for the upper shank (2 in, 1/8 in), rail_w / rail_t (2 in, 1/8 in), cross_w / cross_t (2 in, 1/8 in). Positions: the lower shank's centreline stays at z = 9 in from x = 9 in back to the riser. The ladder's top surface stays at 18 in (the box floor): rails at y = +/-30 in and the front and back cross members all have their tops at 18 in, between x = -18 and -57 in, with the cross members' outer faces flush with those ends. The upper shank runs along y = 0 from the riser back to x = -57 in with its top touching the underside of the cross members. The riser is a vertical tube at x = -7 in joining the lower shank to the upper shank. Everything must stay one connected solid whatever the tube sizes. Also add a function members(params), next to build(params), returning the centrelines as a list of dicts: {'name', 'group' (one of shank, riser, upper_shank, rails, cross), 'a': (x, y, z), 'b': (x, y, z) in world mm, 'outer': tube width in mm, 'wall': wall thickness in mm}, one per member: lower shank, riser, upper shank, the two rails, and the front and back cross members. Keep the script compact: one helper that makes a hollow tube between two points.

build() still makes solid bars: the steel comes to about 1064 cubic inches (302 lb), and the wall-thickness PARAMS (shank_t, riser_t, upper_t, rail_t, cross_t) are ignored. Make every member a hollow square tube with open ends, using its wall thickness, with one compact helper that makes a hollow tube between two points (outer box minus an inner box that is longer than the tube, so the ends are open). Keep members() and all positions exactly as they are. At these sizes the steel should come to roughly 260-300 cubic inches (about 75-85 lb), and the frame must stay one connected solid.

The frame is now 12 separate bodies: the inner cut-outs that open each tube's ends are slicing through the neighbouring members where they meet. Fix the order of operations: make each member as its own finished hollow tube first (outer box minus an inner box that sticks out only 1 mm past that tube's own ends), and only then union the finished tubes together. Never subtract anything after the union. Keep members(), all positions, sizes and PARAMS exactly as they are; it must come out as one connected solid.

Still 9 separate bodies. The reason: where a hollow tube's end butts against another tube, they only TOUCH along a thin wall ring, and the CAD kernel does not fuse solids that merely touch. Make them overlap instead: wherever a member ends against another, extend that tube into the other one by the other tube's wall thickness plus 1 mm (the riser into both shanks, the upper shank into the riser and into the cross members, the rails into the cross members). Keep each tube's inside hollow only along its own length. members(), the centrelines, sizes and PARAMS stay exactly as they are; only the solids overlap at the joints. It must come out as one connected solid.
